    Replacement course ‘prepared’ for DP World Tour Championship

    By Josh Lees • Published: 19 hours ago
    • 4 min read

    Share this article

    Link copied!

    Sign up for our email newsletters

    Get the latest news, reviews, analysis and opinion, plus unmissable deals and exclusive offers. Please check the box of every email you wish to receive.

    Thank you for signing up!

    0:00 / 5:15
    Instaread

    One of the DP World Tour’s previous host courses in Spain is on hold to help put on the circuit’s season-ending Tour Championship amid unrest in the Middle East.

    Dubai has been the long-time host of the DP World Tour’s season finale, and this was expanded to a two-event playoff system with the addition of the Abu Dhabi Championship in 2024.

    Both events play a huge role in the circuit’s calendar, but uncertainty has loomed over the tournaments in recent months amid ongoing tension in the Middle East.

    Matt Fitzpatrick raised this point at the BMW PGA Championship this month. “Being completely honest as things stand right now, I would say I’m not that comfortable,” Fitzpatrick said of the prospect of defending his crown at the DP World Tour Championship in Dubai in November.

    In the aftermath, a spokesperson for the tour said: “It remains our intention to play as scheduled in the UAE but we continue to monitor the situation and take advice from our international travel advisors.”

    Two weeks on, this stance remains the same.

    • The 22 LIV golfers playing the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship

    • Relegated LIV golfer sets sights on the DP World Tour

    Despite this, those in charge have still lined up an alternative, if advice on the Middle East is to change. It emerged that this alternative was to take the season finale to Spain, more specifically Real Club De Golf Sotogrande, a previous home of the Andalucia Masters and Spanish Open.

    At the prospect of being required to step in, Sotogrande General Manager, Kostka Horno Elósegui told bunkered.co.uk: “We have been in discussions with the DP World Tour for some time regarding the different options available to them.

    “Sotogrande was one of the venues the tour was interested in and, after a number of conversations, we were able to reach an agreement that balances the tour’s operational requirements with the needs of our Club and, importantly, our members.

    “We are here to support the tour during this period of uncertainty, and once we understood what would be required from us, the decision to collaborate was relatively straightforward.”

    Plans are in place to start a tournament build at the Spanish course in mid-October as a precaution, but there is no hard cut-off point in place in regard to if the venue will be needed or not.

    “There is no specific deadline that I can share,” the GM added.

    Discussions between those at the tour and Sotogrande started in late August, weeks before players such as Fitzpatrick raised their concerns earlier this month.

    • Patrick Reed’s Race to Dubai hopes hit by fresh injury blow

    • 14 finalists for World Golf Hall of Fame revealed

    Two weeks on, the Englishman seemed more at ease with the prospect of teeing it up in the UAE amid conversations with tour bosses.

    “The tour are getting good advice,” he said at the Alfred Dunhill Links Championship on Wednesday. “I’ve spoken to a few people over the last couple weeks to be honest and they were very reassuring in what’s going on over there.”

    The recently crowned French Open champion admitted he was now taking things ‘week-by-week’. In the build-up to Fitzpatrick’s press conference at St Andrews, the DP World Tour announced a title sponsor for Abu Dhabi Championship, with real estate development company Aldar coming on board.

    “I cannot comment on what may happen with the Abu Dhabi event,” said Horno Elósegui. “Our agreement specifically relates to being available to the DP World Tour in the hypothetical event that the tournament in Dubai cannot take place as planned.”

    The acquisition of an Abu Dhabi-based sponsor, alongside the commitment of Rory McIlroy is as good a sign as any that the DP World Tour still plans to head to the Middle East in just over a month.

    Additionally, the tour’s feeder circuit, the HotelPlanner Tour, finds itself in the region this week for the rescheduled Abu Dhabi Challenge. Originally set to take place in April, the event was delayed until September due to the conflict earlier in the year.

    This week, though, it is business as usual. “I live in the UAE, so this feels like a home tournament for me,” Alex Levy, who is in the field at Al Ain Equestrian, Shooting & Golf Club, told bunkered.co.uk. “I’m very happy to be here, and there’s absolutely nothing to worry about. Life is back to normal here.”

    All roads are seemingly leading towards the Middle East for the DP World Tour, but those in Spain remain on hold should they be needed. “We are working closely with the tour,” Horno Elósegui explained. “Preparing ourselves so that we are ready should they need us.”
